external_sources.title: Article 6ter: How International Law Protects EUCLID's Name and Emblem - EUCLID (Euclid University)
external_sources.content:
Countries bound by Article 6ter must refuse or invalidate the registration of trademarks that contain or imitate a protected name or emblem, unless the organization has authorized it. They must also prohibit its unauthorized use as a trademark where that use would suggest a connection with the organization that does not exist, or would mislead the public. In practical terms, no one may legitimately present a business, a diploma mill or a lookalike website under the EUCLID name or emblem. [...] The procedure is public and documented. The organization asks WIPO to communicate its signs to the States party to the Paris Convention and to the members of the WTO. WIPO publishes the communication in its Article 6ter Express database, and the date of publication counts as the date of receipt for every country. Each State then has twelve months in which it may object. Once communicated, the signs are protected in every State that has not objected.

## What the protection means in practice [...] Article 6ter is not a trademark and cannot be bought or registered by a company, a foundation or a private university. It exists to protect the symbols of public international authority. A State may communicate its own emblems; an intergovernmental organization, created by an agreement between States, may communicate its name, abbreviation and emblem. A purely private institution has no access to this mechanism, whatever its size or reputation.

The provision applies equally to armorial bearings, flags, other emblems, [...] Under Article 6 ter, each member country or international intergovernmental organization (IGO) may communicate armorial bearings, emblems, official signs and hallmarks indicating warranty and control, and names and abbreviations of IGOs to the IB, who will transmit the communications to the other member countries. Within twelve months from receipt of the notification, a member country may transmit its objections, through the IB. external_sources.title: Editorial Policy - TradingKey
external_sources.content:
Our expert financial writers contribute deep insights, which are reviewed by our professional editors, fact-checkers, and compliance officers to ensure that our core values of professionalism, accuracy, and objectivity are consistently upheld throughout the creation process. [...] Our editorial team works around the clock, monitoring authoritative sources, evaluating content, cross-referencing and double-checking data and facts—avoiding errors at the source and presenting users with objective, well-substantiated content.  
Our financial expert team calibrates each piece for both professional rigour and neutrality. We reject vague, biased, or misleading expressions, ensuring every viewpoint offered is clear, rigorous, and impartial—truly honouring users’ trust. [...] With academic backgrounds in finance, economics, or journalism, our editorial team is proficient and professional in macroeconomic policies, capital markets, and financial analysis. Every article is the result of a collaborative effort based on a strict multi-level review process—Editor-Senior Editor-Chief Editor—to deliver accuracy, readability, and timeliness.
